slides.headline: October 4, 1977: India's External Affairs Minister became the first person to address the UN General Assembly in Hindi.
Atal Bihari Vajpayee addressed the UN General Assembly's 32nd session entirely in Hindi
slides.body: As India's External Affairs Minister, Vajpayee broke with decades of English-only precedent at the UN podium, speaking on nuclear disarmament and economic cooperation among developing nations - and invoking the ancient Indian idea of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, 'the world is one family.'

slides.headline: It remains one of the only times Hindi has ever been spoken from the UN's main podium.
slides.body: Decades before 'India's voice at the UN' became a familiar phrase in diplomacy, Vajpayee used the moment to assert that India's own language belonged on the world's biggest diplomatic stage - not just its ideas in someone else's words.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat speaks to the world in its own voice, literally.
slides.body: Vajpayee's 1977 speech stands as an early marker of India choosing self-assurance over convention on the global stage - the same instinct a developed India will need by 2047.
